system.one_liner: Multi-level reinforcement learning: a human-inspired policy loss pushes the policy away from experiences of different rating levels, on top of rating-based RL (RbRL).

content.variant_note: an RL agent and environment loop with a human-rating branch (RbRL, blue region), extended by a second region that turns rated buffers into distributions and a policy loss returned to the agent
content.argues: Rated experiences can shape a policy loss as well as a reward: samples of each rating level become distributions that the policy is pushed away from, most strongly for low ratings.
content.subject: RbRL's agent, environment and human ratings, plus the new rating-induced policy loss built from per-rating buffers and distributions.

content.reading_order: Starts at the Environment and RL Agent loop in the blue region, follows the arrows to the rated Segments (Bad, Good), crosses by dashed arrows to the peach region's buffers, distributions and loss, then the long arrow back to the RL Agent.

layout.arrangement_note: Two large rounded regions side by side on white: a blue RbRL region on the left (about 60% of the width) and a peach Rating-induced Policy Loss region on the right. In the blue region the Environment (top-left), the RL Agent (bottom-left) and a big Segments box with Bad and Good groups (right) are joined by vertical and horizontal arrows, with a person icon above Segments. In the peach region two buffer boxes with distribution glyphs sit above the policy-loss box, and a long arrow returns from the loss across both regions to the RL Agent.

lessons.what_to_learn: To show how a new component plugs into an existing method, draw the existing method as one tinted region and the new component as a second region of another tint, join them with the few arrows that cross the border, and keep a class colour on every item of that class.
lessons.suits: Extensions of a known algorithm (RL, RLHF, contrastive learning) where the figure must show both the known loop and what the new loss adds.

summary: The paper proposes multi-level reinforcement learning, in which a human-inspired policy loss pushes the policy away from experiences of different rating levels, on top of rating-based RL (RbRL). Figure 1 draws two rounded regions side by side. The blue RbRL region shows an RL Agent and an Environment joined by Action and Observation arrows, a human icon rating trajectory Segments into Bad (orange) and Good (green) groups of robot-arm glyphs, and Reward Learning feeding the agent. The peach region, Rating-induced Policy Loss, sorts the groups into Buffer 0 and Buffer 1, turns them into Distribution 0 and 1 hub glyphs and feeds a loss box that pushes away from low ratings, whose long arrow returns to the RL Agent.
summary_zh: 论文提出多级强化学习：在基于评分的 RL（RbRL）之上，用受人启发的策略损失让策略远离不同评级的经验。图左蓝区是 RbRL：智能体、环境、人给片段打分，分成“差”“好”两组；图右橙区把两组存入缓冲、转成分布并生成损失，回传给智能体。
notes: The arrow labelled Action points from the Environment to the RL Agent and the one labelled Observation points back (confirmed in the SVG arrowheads); relations are recorded as drawn. The role of the two rows inside each Buffer is taken from the paper text, not from the figure. Only two rating levels are drawn.
